title: Learning bass and tuba fingering from Billy Taylor
summary: Watching Billy Taylor, he finds bass fingers like violin and works out how tuba valves correspond to trombone positions.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: That's when I started fooling with the bass fiddle, when Billy Taylor was there.
-- and I used to watch him. Then I
found out that it fingered just as on the back of a violin, you see.
Oh, that's why you came in on that thing. I see.
Yes, because I know you had and I (unintelligible) did some things later.

-- so I used to fool with Billy's bass and then he had a tuba. Well, then I got to fooling with this tuba, too, and I found it dawned on me that the B-flat instruments were all relative. All the notes he made open on the tuba I could make closed on the first position on the trombone, you see.

Oh, definitely, you know. And your second valve was my second position, the third valve was the first -- is the first valve -- the third position, rather, and your fourth position was your first and second valve. Your fifth position is your second and third valve and your first and third valves is the sixth position, and all three valves down is the seventh position in the trombone. And it's the same way with the tuba.
Yeah, you really wiggled it out.
So after you find this out, then you say, oh, gee, you know, I can play this.
